The settlement shows the payment with a fee of 226,000 paise and tax of 40,680 paise. The payment was settled on 2026-09-15. This confirms it's one of the payment rows in the settlement.

Now let me consider alternative patterns. The most straightforward alternative would be using a different subset of invoices. Option 1 - **[INV-00119, INV-00121, INV-00178]** - represents a "many_to_one" pattern (3 invoices from different customers/students) but only covers 3 of the 4 named students.

The most defensible alternative is **option 5: [INV-00015, INV-00119, INV-00120, INV-00121]** which still maintains:
- Exactly 4 invoices (matching 4 students mentioned)
- Exactly ₹113,000 sum
- All issued around the same time (Sep 5-8)

However, this substitutes Anika Das for Pari Das, which contradicts the explicit notes. Let me instead propose an alternative based on a **split_settlement** or **many_to_one** pattern using one of the 3-invoice combinations:

input.rationale: Alternative reconciliation of the same ₹113,000 loan disbursal payment as a consolidation of three invoices from different loan beneficiaries: Om Agarwal (₹18,000), Priya Malhotra (₹45,000), and Riya Das (₹50,000). This represents a many-to-one pattern where the lender's disbursement covered multiple student invoices across the portfolio, though it doesn't account for all four named students explicitly mentioned in the payment notes, it achieves an exact arithmetic match with an alternative subset of the available invoices."
